title: Voitaikina (Puff Paste)
description: Prepared with gin, juice, and butter.
steps: Wash the butter in ice water and force the water out by wrapping the butter tightly into a towel.
Whip the egg, add water, lemon juice, gin and flour mixed with 1 teaspoon of butter.
Knead with fingers to an even paste.
Roll, place on top of the paste the butter flattened to a cake.
Fold up the sheet of paste so as to enclose the butter.
Place on ice in a dish for 1 hour.
Roll the paste into an oblong square and fold in three.
Turn over, reroll and fold in three again.
Repeat this operation three times rolling out twice and folding up three times each time.
Place the paste on ice for 15 minutes between each operation.
Rerolling must be done in the opposite direction.
Bake in a hot oven.

steps: The flour is sifted, a portion of it is worked well together with the milk and the yeast stirred with 2 tsk. sugar.

The cake is turned out, the mold is filled halfway with sugar syrup, the savarin is placed in and is allowed to stand until it has absorbed all the syrup, then it is turned out of the mold and placed on a flat cake plate with cake paper.

Garnish the baskets with whipped cream and top with a small star of candied orange peel.

steps: Rinse the apricots and soak them in water for 1 hour.
Put them on to cook in the water in which they have been soaked.
Add the sugar and let the apricots cook until completely soft.
Thicken the soup with the potato flour mixed in a little cold water, give it a good boil, and serve with whipped cream.

title: Aprikossås (Apricot Sauce)
description: A sauce made with apricots, water, and sugar.
steps: The apricots are rinsed in lukewarm water and are then allowed to soak for 2-3 hours in the water in which they are to be cooked.
They are then brought to a boil together with the sugar until they are completely soft, after which they are pressed through a sieve.
The sauce is brought to a boil, diluted with a little water if necessary, is allowed to cool and is served.

title: Arter med Fläsk (Pea Soup with Pork)
description: A soup made with peas, salt or pork or brisket, and water.

ingredients.name: 750 grams salt-cured pork loin or brisket

steps: The peas are cleaned and rinsed well, and if they are considered hard to cook, they are placed the evening before in the water in which they are to be cooked
If the pork is heavily salted, it should lie in cold water for several hours, otherwise it is only rinsed, placed in cold water, skimmed and allowed to cook through for about 2 hours
Peas are always added in cold water; if the water is hard, it is boiled up before use and allowed to cool
The peas are allowed to boil up slowly, but then cook quickly for the first hour, as the skins loosen more easily
They are thinned with cold water and when the skins float up they are immediately skimmed off
The skins should be carefully removed, as this makes the soup less coarse and tastes better
After 1.5 to 2 hours, the broth from the pork is added, which should first be tasted, and the peas are allowed to cook until they begin to fall apart
They are seasoned with salt and, if desired, with a little marjoram or ginger
The pork is cut into slices and served separately
Leftover pea soup can be made into purée, but then 2 deciliters more peas should be taken when the soup is cooked

title: Arter med Fläsk (Pea Soup with Pork)
description: A soup made with peas, pork or brisket, and water.

ingredients.name: 750 gr. salted pork loin or brisket

steps: Clean and rinse the peas well. If they are considered hard to cook, soak them the night before in the water they are to be cooked in.
If the pork is heavily salted, let it soak in cold water for several hours, otherwise just rinse it. Place it in cold water, skim, and let it cook about 2 hours until done.
Always add peas to cold water. If the water is hard, boil it first and let it cool.

Let the peas come to a boil slowly, then boil rapidly for the first hour so the skins loosen more easily. Add cold water and when the skins float up, skim them away immediately. Remove the skins carefully as this makes the soup less grainy and better tasting.
After 1 1/2-2 hours, add the pork broth that has been tasted beforehand, and let the peas cook until they begin to fall apart. Season with salt and, if desired, with a little marjoram or ginger.
Slice the pork and serve separately.

title: Artistkompott (Artist's Compote)
description: Prepared with sugar syrup, port wine, and apples.

steps: Mix the sugar syrup (see sugar syrup for compote) with the wine in a compote bowl.

description: A soup made with jerusalem artichokes, broth, and egg yolks.
steps: Rinse the Jerusalem artichokes well and scrape them, preferably under running water.
Shape them round and place them in vinegar-mixed water (1 tablespoon vinegar, 1 liter water) so they do not become dark.
After 1 hour, place them in boiling, salted water and let them cook until tender, then place them in the soup bowl; reserve the broth, which should be about 1/2 liter.

title: Bajersk Kräm med Choklad (Bavarian Cream with Chocolate)
description: Prepared with chocolate, cream, and vanilla bean.

ingredients.name: 1 dcl. hot water for the gelatin

steps: Cook the sugar with the water and vanilla until a clear, simmering syrup forms, then remove the vanilla bean.
Melt the chocolate in a water bath, without the addition of water, and stir it into the sugar syrup.
Rinse the gelatin in cold water, dissolve it in the hot water and add it, then stir the cream until it is cold.
Then fold in the cream whipped to stiff peaks, and pour the cream into a water-rinsed and sugar-sprinkled mold and let it stand on ice for 2-3 hours to set.
When the cream is to be served, loosen it from the edge with a pointed knife and turn it out onto a flat glass dish with cake paper.
The cream can also be poured into a mold with a lid and frozen, but then only 3 sheets of gelatin are used.
